title: Anthropic IPO, the largest AI listing
since_label: Tue 10 Nov, when the price range was set
status: CNBC reports Anthropic was indicated to open at $105 against its $83 IPO price, with Hyperliquid perps above $104, and Yahoo Finance reports indications later rose to $110, but no first trade had been reported at last check. Bloomberg reports the Nasdaq 100 rose 2% early on the debut and Stock Titan reports tech gave up most of those gains by late morning; the first-day close is still open.
why: A raise this size absorbs cash that would otherwise chase other risk, and its first-day close reprices every AI name.
next_label: First trade and first-day close as ANT
sources: Anthropic, CNBC, Yahoo Finance, Bloomberg, Stock Titan, CNN

title: Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, Kress named interim
since_label: Fri 6 Nov close, the last price before the weekend reports
status: CNBC reports interim CEO Colette Kress told staff at the first all-hands on Wed 18 Nov to move forward and mentioned pay raises, Invezz reports the shares fell 2.89% to $150.96 that day, and Investrade reports Nvidia rose about 3% early Thu in a chip rebound before the Anthropic debut. NBC News reports chair Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Huang and has hired Heidrick & Struggles to look at internal and external candidates, with no timetable yet for a permanent CEO.
why: Nvidia is the anchor of the AI trade and one of the heaviest weights in the Nasdaq, which alts follow.
sources: Nvidia, CNBC, NBC News, Invezz, Investrade, CNN

title: Iran and US trade strikes in the Gulf
since_label: Thu 12 Nov 00:00 UTC, before Iran reported the Sirik strike
status: CBS News, citing Reuters, reports Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed two more tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Thu 19 Nov, and Gulf News reports JMIC recorded four tanker attacks in 96 hours and the Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi missile. CNN reports a third US carrier group has joined blockade and escort operations, GB News reports Qatar says mediation was continuing, and no ceasefire has been reported.
why: CoinDesk cites the Gulf escalation, with the dollar and Fed hike odds, behind the crypto sell-off; oil feeds straight into rate expectations.
sources: CBS News, Reuters, Gulf News, CNN, GB News, NewsNation, CoinDesk

title: MSCI drops Strategy from its indexes
since_label: Wed 11 Nov close, before MSCI's after-hours announcement
status: Investing.com reports analysts estimate passive funds must sell about 13 million Strategy shares, roughly $1.6 billion, before the MSCI deletion takes effect after the close on 30 Nov, and Nexo reports bitcoin recovered toward $64,000 on Thu 19 Nov after $306M of net US spot ETF outflows on Wed, citing SoSoValue. Benzinga reports Strategy bought only 485 BTC last week while directing money to STRC buybacks, and it is still open whether other index providers will follow.
why: Strategy is the largest corporate BTC holder, and forced selling of its shares tests the main route equity money takes into bitcoin.
sources: MSCI, Strategy, Investing.com, Nexo, Benzinga, Cryptonomist

title: Binance $6.3B hack, stolen ETH on the move
since_label: Thu 29 Oct 00:00 UTC, before the hack was reported
status: CoinDesk, citing Reuters, reports an Abu Dhabi court granted Binance a worldwide order freezing proceeds of the 29 Oct theft, which the FBI attributes to North Korea's TraderTraitor, with a hearing on 1 Dec on whether 18 firms must hand over assets they have frozen. Cointelegraph, citing Lookonchain, reports the hacker moved another 137,600 ETH, about $248M, on Thu 19 Nov, and Binance says it has already replaced customer assets from its own funds.
why: Stolen ETH that no issuer can freeze is being moved and swapped, a supply overhang for ETH and alts while crypto sentiment sits at extreme fear.
next_label: Abu Dhabi court hearing on frozen assets
sources: Binance, Reuters, CoinDesk, The Block, Bitcoin Magazine, The National
